memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system codebase, memory-retrieve.sh, memory-harvest.sh, events-query.sh, and events-append.sh all resolve PROJECT_ROOT as `cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd`. Because BASH_SOURCE[0] is the literal invocation string, and every call site invokes them as the relative path `bash .claude/scripts/{name}.sh`, a chained `cd "$TARGET_ROOT" && bash .claude/scripts/{name}.sh ...` (same Bash tool call) correctly redirects PROJECT_ROOT to $TARGET_ROOT with zero script changes. An absolute-path invocation, or a `cd` issued in an earlier Bash tool call, defeats this silently.

Claude Code's standard OTel resource attributes (monitoring-usage docs, verified 2026-07) are session.id, user.id, user.email, user.account_uuid, user.account_id, organization.id, app.version, app.entrypoint, terminal.type -- cwd is NOT among them. Every Claude Code hook, however, DOES receive both session_id (same UUIDv4 as OTel's session.id) and cwd on every invocation's JSON stdin (common fields: session_id, prompt_id, transcript_path, cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name). A hook is therefore the correct bridge point for capturing cwd/session correlation that OTel itself does not carry by default.

In agent-system's unified event store, events-log-lifecycle.sh (Stop/SubagentStop) and events-log-artifact.sh (PostToolUse) both already parse full hook stdin JSON but only extract narrow fields (agent_id/last_assistant_message; file_path respectively) -- they discard the session_id/cwd fields the hooks contract guarantees are present on every invocation. Any future cross-source correlation work in this codebase can extend these two existing hooks rather than registering new ones.
